findings.title: doneRetroChecks' missing/empty-file branch has no test, and its semantics silently changed
findings.detail: doneRetroChecks (new in this diff) replaced the old fileNonEmpty(retro.md) check with an inline os.ReadFile + strings.TrimSpace(...) == "" check. This is a real behaviour change: fileNonEmpty only checks file size > 0 (facts.go:41-44), so a whitespace-only retro.md previously passed this gate and would have been hashed/recorded; now it is refused as "missing or empty". None of the new tests (TestDoneRetroRefusesUnfilledProseSlot, TestDoneRetroRefusesARecordedRetroInExecute, TestDoneRetroAcceptedInArchivedPhase) or any existing test writes a missing/empty/whitespace-only retro.md while in the finish or archived phase, so this branch and its behaviour change are completely unexercised by the suite.

findings.title: `got["ignored"] != nil` assertions are tautological on the failure path
findings.detail: In TestDoneRetroRefusesUnfilledProseSlot (line 306) and TestDoneRetroRefusesARecordedRetroInExecute (line 346), the refusal assertions check `code != 1 || got["ignored"] != nil`. `got` is unmarshalled only from stdout (cmd_init_test.go:17-33), while `fail()` writes exclusively to stderr (cli.go:158-161), so on any refusal (code 1) stdout is empty and `got` is nil — `got["ignored"]` can never be non-nil here. The check adds no real coverage of the 'must not be marked ignored' intent; the actual no-new-receipt guarantee is (correctly) covered separately via countEvents before/after.
